response.text: Consumer fireworks may be discharged in the City only on Victoria Day or Canada Day, or on a day covered by a special occasions fireworks discharge permit issued by the Fire Chief [2]. On those days, discharge must end by 11:00 p.m. [2]. If weather makes discharge impractical or unsafe, the designated day moves to the next day before or after [2]. Discharge on your own property is permitted only if you are the owner or have the owner's written consent, and it must not occur within 100 metres of certain places such as explosives storage [2]. Fireworks may not be discharged indoors, in a manner creating a nuisance or unsafe condition, or contrary to the manufacturer's instructions [2][1]. A fireworks discharge permit is not required on Victoria Day or Canada Day [1]. The passages do not cover whether any other backyard restrictions apply beyond these.

Consumer fireworks may only be discharged in the City on Victoria Day or Canada Day, and not after 11:00 p.m. on those days [2]. If weather makes it impractical or unsafe, the next day before or after those holidays becomes the designated day, with the same 11:00 p.m. cutoff [2]. Any other day requires a special occasions fireworks discharge permit from the Fire Chief [2][3]. You also cannot discharge fireworks on land you don't own or occupy without the owner's prior written consent [2]. The passages don't address the specific time of day for days other than these holidays.

Consumer fireworks may be discharged in the City only on Victoria Day or Canada Day, or on a day covered by a special occasions fireworks discharge permit issued by the Fire Chief [2]. On those days, discharge must stop by 11:00 p.m. [2]. If weather makes discharge impractical or unsafe, the designated day moves to the next day before or after, with the same 11:00 p.m. limit [2]. A permit is not needed for consumer fireworks on Victoria Day or Canada Day, or the weather-altered day [1]. Discharge on land you don't own requires the owner's prior written consent [2], and you must keep fire extinguishing equipment ready at the site [2]. The passages do not cover whether a permit is needed for a backyard on a day other than these, beyond the special occasions permit described above.

Yes. No one may excavate for or erect a swimming pool without first obtaining a permit from the Executive Director for a swimming pool enclosure for the proposed pool [1]. The application must include the fee set out in Chapter 441, Fees and Charges, and plans showing the pool's location relative to lot lines and adjacent buildings, complete details of the enclosure, and any other information the Executive Director requires [1]. If you are still building the pool, you may use temporary fencing meeting the stated specifications, but the pool cannot be filled or used until an officer inspects and confirms a permanent enclosure that fully complies [1]. The passages do not cover any requirements for discharging pool water, which are separate from the enclosure permit.

Yes. No one may excavate for or erect a swimming pool without first obtaining a permit from the Executive Director for a swimming pool enclosure for the proposed pool [1]. The application must be in the required form, include the fee set out in Chapter 441, and include plans showing the pool's location relative to lot lines and adjacent buildings, complete details of the enclosure, and any other required information [1]. The permit will be refused if the enclosure would contravene the enclosure by-law or other applicable law [1]. While the pool is under construction, temporary fencing may be allowed if authorized, and it must be replaced with a permanent enclosure when an officer directs or construction is substantially complete, whichever is first [1]. The passages do not cover whether a separate permit is needed for wastewater discharge when the pool is drained, or the details of the City's pre-application or fee requirements beyond what is stated here.

Yes. No one may excavate for or erect a swimming pool without first obtaining a permit from the Executive Director for a swimming pool enclosure for the proposed pool [1]. The application must include the non-refundable fee set out in Chapter 441, plus plans showing the pool's location relative to lot lines and adjacent buildings, complete details of the enclosure, and any other information the Executive Director requires [1]. Temporary fencing during construction may be allowed with authorization, but the pool cannot be filled with water until an officer has inspected and confirmed a permanent compliant enclosure, or, if temporary fencing is used, the pool cannot be used until permanent fencing is inspected and confirmed [1]. The passages do not cover your pool's wastewater discharge requirements for when you drain or maintain it beyond the general rules, nor the enclosure's specific construction standards in detail.
